quiz.problem: The feedback treats the move from needs-info back to needs-triage as automatic, and that is wrong. In the Skill nothing relabels the issue when the reporter replies. That is exactly why its third attention bucket is "needs-info with reporter activity": the issue still carries needs-info until triage re-evaluates it with you. The Lesson's own line 270 says the automation lives in Matt's repo workflows, not in the Skill. So option b ("stays in needs-info until you remove the label by hand") is half true on a local Markdown tracker. The right option's feedback also contradicts itself: it says the issue went back to needs-triage, then cites the needs-info-with-replies bucket.
quiz.evidence: SKILL.md lists the bucket "`needs-info` with reporter activity since the last triage notes". The option b feedback reads "The state machine sends it back when the reporter replies". The option c feedback reads "needs-info issues with new replies are one of the three attention buckets". Lesson line 270 says "That automation belongs to his repo, not the Skill".
quiz.fix:
Ask about the state machine's next state rather than the mechanism, and replace b:
```test predict-reporter-replies
An issue has sat in `needs-info` for a week. The reporter finally replies with exact steps. Under the Skill's state machine, where does the issue go next?
- [ ] Straight to `ready-for-agent`, because the missing information has arrived.
  > New information still has to be evaluated, and the claim verified, before anything is agent-ready.
- [ ] To `ready-for-human`, because a person supplied the missing details.
  > Who supplied the details doesn't set the state. `ready-for-human` is for work an agent can't do, and nobody has evaluated this yet.
- [x] Back to `needs-triage`, for another look with the new steps.
  > Right. The next time you ask what needs attention, it's listed, and triage reads its earlier notes so it doesn't re-ask anything.
- [ ] To `wontfix`, because a week without an answer means the report has gone stale.
  > The reporter did answer. Auto-closing silent issues is something Matt's own repo automates, not the Skill.
```

quiz.problem: The distractors give the answer away by shape. Options c and d each leave out a step (c has no recommend, d has no grill), so a reader can drop them without knowing the order. Wording differs too ("apply the outcome" in a, "apply outcome" elsewhere).
quiz.evidence: a: "Recommend → gather context → grill if needed → verify → apply the outcome". c: "Gather context → grill → apply outcome → verify" (4 steps). d: "Verify → apply outcome → recommend → gather context" (4 steps). SKILL.md step 3 starts "Before any grilling".
quiz.fix:
Give all four options the same five steps, each wrong option with one error (equal lengths pass the lint, which only flags a unique longest):
```test sequence-one-item
Triage is looking at a stranger's report that the export button crashes the app. In what order does it work through the report?
- [ ] Gather context → recommend → grill if needed → verify → apply outcome
  > Verification comes before any grilling, so you never spend questions fleshing out a claim that turns out to be false.
- [x] Gather context → recommend → verify → grill if needed → apply outcome
  > Right. Read and check first, recommend and wait, prove the claim, flesh it out if needed, then act.
- [ ] Gather context → verify → grill if needed → apply outcome → recommend
  > Triage recommends and waits for your direction before it verifies or applies anything. Recommending last would mean acting without you.
- [ ] Recommend → gather context → verify → grill if needed → apply outcome
  > It can't recommend before it has read the issue and checked the code.
```
